jamie: Quick follow-up on the precision routing contract we sketched in the RFC — trying to lock down semantics for the runtime <-> kernel handshake for mixed-precision attention (FP8/INT8/INT4). Want to avoid surprises during rollout.

arjun: +1. main open Q for me: should kernels be allowed to change effective dtype mid-call (e.g., read INT8 kv, upcast to FP16 for matmul, then write FP8 cache) or must they preserve declared storage dtype?

maria: prefer explicit: kernels must declare input storage dtype and output storage dtype. runtime can only assume what kernel advertises. if a kernel internally upcasts that's opaque, as long as read/write contracts hold. makes rollout reasoning simpler.

lee: that seems right. also need a clear contract around kv-cache layout/alignment — INT4 packs require different stride and bit offsets. runtime needs to know: (1) element bits, (2) stride in bytes, (3) alignment requirement, (4) whether tail bits are zeroed.

arjun: agree on kv layout metadata. also: fallback semantics. if a request routes to a model variant that doesn't support INT4, we either: convert at routing (dequant->float->quant) or fall back to a compatible kernel. both have perf/cost tradeoffs. we should specify preferred order.

sri: can we codify an ordered list on policy: (a) exact kernel match, (b) compatible kernel with no data transform (same storage layout), (c) kernel-level implicit dequant/quant (allowed only if kernel advertises idempotent transforms), (d) runtime data transform (expensive). runtime picks first available.

maria: +1 to ordered policy, but we need to be strict about (c). "implicit dequant/quant" sounds scary for determinism. require deterministic, bit-exact reversible transforms, and a flag kernel.can_implicit_transform=true. also need an opt-out per-customer.

jamie: good call. another area: fused dequant for attention path. If we allow kernels to accept quantized QKV and produce dequantized matmul stream internally and then fuse softmax+scale back into quant path, we save memory and copy. But then debug/telemetry (per-token latency breakdown, token-level perf) becomes opaque. Thoughts?

arjun: fused path is big win. proposal: add a trace hook interface kernels must call at key steps: "kv_load", "qk_matmul_start", "qk_matmul_end", "softmax_start", "softmax_end", "write_kv". hooks are lightweight callbacks the runtime can enable for debugging. default no-op.

lee: careful: hooks must be async-safe (no allocations) and optionally gather only counters (cycles, bytes). we shouldn't let kernels block on runtime for tracing.

maria: also we need to record quality metrics when kernel does any lossy quant/transform. add kernel.report_quality_delta(tag, delta_metric_name). runtime can aggregate and tie to eval prompt sets.

sri: ops-bot: deploy-check?

ops-bot: deploy-check: no active deploys in eng-runtime for the next 2 hours. CI: unit tests for layout metadata and hook smoke tests required.

jamie: action items from this thread: (1) arjun to draft the precise kernel metadata proto (dtype_in, dtype_out, bits_per_elem, stride_bytes, alignment, can_implicit_transform, can_fuse_dequant, hooks_supported) — due EOD Fri; (2) lee to sketch hook API semantics and async safety constraints — due Wed; (3) maria to propose a safe rollout plan + customer opt-out flag; (4) sri to add CI smoke tests in runtime for fallback ordering. i'll prepare a short doc we can attach to the RFC.

arjun: I'll include example proto and a tiny compatibility matrix for common GPUs.

maria: will draft rollout + opt-out language.

lee: ok will design hook shape and a small C header for kernels.

sri: will add tests.

jamie: thanks all. if anyone sees a blocker (especially legal/regulatory for per-customer opt-out) call it out here. plan to merge contract doc into RFC next Tue.
